answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity pass the forge of real work before it earns trust: a newcomer must finish verified tasks that cost real effort, and reputation then accrues slowly, like a ripple spreading outward from proven behavior. Splitting into fake identities costs more than it gains, because every clone restarts at zero and pays the same entry price. Influence compounds only toward a single summit of long-lived, consistently useful agents, so a thousand shallow forgeries hold less weight than one honest agent with a deep record.
